title.narrative: Area-based food production support 2024 - Provision of FSL, Protection, NFI, Health and Nutrition Assistance in Saraf Omra locality, North Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project's objective is to provide integrated lifesaving Health, Nutrition, ES/INFs, FSL and Protection services for affected and vulnerable people in Saraf Omra locality of North Darfur state. The project will address the immediate needs of affected people through lifesaving activities of Health, Nutrition, ES/INFs, FSL and Protection. The lifesaving needs of aboutnbsp71,253nbsppeople (16,427 men, 21,819 women, 15,871 boys, and 17,136nbspgirls) will be addressed through integrated Health, Nutrition, ES/INFs, FSL and protectionnbspservices. Specifically, the project will improve access to essential health services, including preventive and curative services, and improve the nutrition of CU5 and pregnant and lactating women by detecting and treating acute malnutrition and promoting best nutrition practices in targeted communities, improving access to NFIs, FSL, and protection.ltbrgtThe health sector delivers essential health services, including outpatient consultations, medical investigations, routine vaccination, maternal and child health care, including risk communication and community engagement, and support referral to secondary health care. The services will include the management of communicable and non-communicable diseases as well as emergency referral services targeting men, women, boys and girls, the elderly, people with disabilities, and children. Services will be provided for free to people in the catchment areas and nearby communities.ltbrgtThe nutrition services will establish and increase access to nutrition interventions, including OTP, TSFP, FBPM, home fortification, distribution of vitamin A and iron supplements, MUAC screening, and IYCN counseling among IDPs and host community members.ltbrgtThe food security component will provide agricultural inputs and training to vulnerable households, prioritizing female-headed families and persons with disabilities, to improve food production and income generation. Concurrently, pastoral communities will benefit from the establishment of livestock protection committees to manage grazing areas, migratory routes, and water resources. These committees will also receive training in conflict resolution to address disputes over shared resources effectively.ltbrgtEmergency shelter interventions will supply plastic sheets and non-food items to displaced families, prioritizing vulnerable groups such as widowed women and individuals who lost their homes.ltbrgtA multi-sectorial approach is used to address cross-cutting issues and provide all recruited staff, engaged contractors, and volunteers oriented on PSEA. PSEA will be included in awareness sessions of the targeted population with information on how and where to report SEA incidents safely.The project will ensure accountabilitynbspto the affected population, including providing the targeted population with access to information on project interventions and beneficiaries through channels and language that beneficiaries access and understand a mechanism to collect their feedback and complaints.ltbrgtnbspltbrgtUPO will be part of the coordination mechanism in the state with relevant cluster partners and stakeholders (WHO, SMOH UNICEF, WFP, UNFPA) for sustainable provision of essentials (drugs and supplies) to avoid interruption or delay of health and nutrition services due to shortage of stock out of medicines and supplies. The outreach activities, such as health education through house-to-house visits by trained volunteers, health education sessions at health facilities, and awareness campaigns, will be provided.ltbrgtlt/pgt
